newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian says he has legal claim in Busang find.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian says he has legal claim in Busang find.

text.p: Indonesian businessman Jusuf Merukh on Wednesday said he was entitled to a 40 percent stake in a disputed gold deposit majority-owned by Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd.
Merukh said he owned a 20 percent stake in the Busang property, which is divided into three sections, and had an option to buy another 20 percent in the spectacular find.
"Indirectly, I have an option to buy a further 20 percent of Bre-X shares in Busang ll and lll (blocks B and C) at cost, which means about $4 million," he told Reuters in an interview.
"This is God-given (the find). There's no hanky-panky," the soft-spoken, U.S.-educated Merukh said in his first public comment on the controversy raging around the find in East Kalimantan.
"By law, I have a right to Busang ll and lll. I want the gold, not the right. I am confident of getting my stake."

Bre-X has estimated gold reserves in the deposit of at least 47 million ounces, which has transformed the Canadian company overnight from a little-known entity to a major player in the mining industry.

Merukh's claim to the Busang property has delayed the Indonesian government's issuance of contracts of work (COWs) to Bre-X until the ownership dispute is resolved. Bre-X needs the COWs for further exploration and development of Busang II and III.
Mining sources said the dispute centred on Merukh's claims on the deposit.
The Director-General of Mining, Kuntoro Mangkusubroto, said on Wednesday the government wanted the dispute settled amicably and said the government would not interfere.

"The government will not interfere in the dispute between Bre-X and its Indonesian partner because it's purely an internal company matter," he told reporters. "We want them to settle the dispute themselves."
Bre-X has said its Indonesian legal adviser had told it that claims by one of its Indonesian partners to an ownership stake in the deposit were without merit. The partner was not identified.
Merukh said he owned a 20-percent stake in Busang l, the original gold find, through two companies he controlled -- PT Krueng Gasui and PT Sungai Atan Perdana.
Eighty percent of Busang l had been owned by Westralian Resource Project, an Australian company.
Merukh said he had signed an agreement with Westralian giving him an option to buy another 20 percent stake.
"Through Krueng Gasui, I had an option to buy another 20 percent stake," he said, adding that he would exercise the option and had informed Bre-X of his intention.
Merukh said Westralian sold its stake in Busang l to Waverly Finance Management of Scotland, which in turn sold it to Bre-X.

"I have a right to Busang ll and lll and I suggest my partner (Bre-X) to negotiate to seek an amicable solution," he said. "When Bre-X bought Westralian's stake (in Busang l), it bought Westralian's assets and liabilities," he said.
Merukh also said he had signed a technical assistance agreement earlier this year with Golden Valley Mines NL of Australia.
"Golden Valley will provide me with technical assistance such as geologists and engineers to participate in the development of the (Busang) project," he said.
"This does not mean that Golden Valley has a share in the property. It will get a royalty, which we are discussing."
Bre-X said in a statement isued in Canada that Golden Valley was not entitled to any part of the Busang property. The Bre-X office in Jakarta refers all queries to the company office in Toronto.
